title: af/TelemetryConfig@2
description: `af telemetry config RUN --json` (telemetry design §7.4, §10; ADR-0153): the configuration record of one run in one execution, assembled from the `config` parts (`af/TelemetryConfig@2` records) that name that run — its run id and its `af.run` span (`run_span_id`) — never another run's of the same execution (a measurement run inside a Task Attempt has its own). The record has three sections in a fixed order, each written as as many parts as the 16 KiB record bound needs: `configuration` (`af --version --json`, layer `version`; the effective configuration, one row per key with the configuration layer it came from and its file, home-relative, and line as `origin` — a value whose origin is the environment layer is `<env>` and its origin the variable's name; the digests of `.af/af.toml` and `.af/af.lock`, layer `policy`) and `machine` (the Provider registry entries with grant paths as placeholders, layer `provider`; the harness versions the preflight probed and the Claude Code managed-settings digests, layer `harness`; the host, layer `host`; the names, never the values, of the `AF_*` and `OTEL_*` variables present, layer `variable`), both written when the run's `af.run` opens; and `plan` (the policy revision, the pipeline's name, digest and nodes, the Task's id, kind and pipeline, layer `policy`; the execution bindings, layer `binding`; a measurement's own identity, layer `measurement`), written when the plan resolves. A section is `complete` when every part from 1 to `parts` is retained and the last is marked complete, `incomplete` when one is missing (`missing_parts`), `unknown` when no part of it is retained (a run refused before its plan resolved has no plan section). `state` is `complete` when every section is, `incomplete` otherwise, `absent` when the run recorded no part in the execution (a level below `spans`). The rows keep the sections' order. Every value passed the credential rules; a secret-named key withholds its value. `texts` lists the texts the record names (`af.config.text`: the pipeline, the Task file, `.af/af.toml`) by digest and size, at every level that records the configuration. Nothing here is evidence.
